results.input: Tell me about the world of Nox: how does its magic work? And what does Kael Draven carry?
results.answer:
I cannot find a character named Kael Draven in the world. The author's story has Aria Voss, Brannoc Hale, and Sera Quill. Did you mean one of them?

As for Nox and magic: the lore documents do not mention a place called Nox. The world I find in the canon is called Aethel. In Aethel, magic works through three disciplines—Fire, Frost, and Aether—each with different powers. Every spell costs mana, which casters have in a limited pool [935211ae, eac3e3c8, aba95d85]. Minor spells cost 5-15 mana, and greater workings are limited to Archmages.

Is Nox a location in Aethel that the author has not yet documented, or would you like to know about one of the three characters instead?
evidence:
[search_lore] passage 935211ae (The Magic of Aethel): Magic in Aethel is paid for in mana. Every spell has a price, every caster has a limited pool, and the places of the world bend the rules in their own ways. This document lists the general laws. Individual places add their own rules, which are described in the location documents.
[search_lore] passage eac3e3c8 (The Magic of Aethel > The Three Disciplines): There are three disciplines of magic. Fire, also called pyromancy, creates and shapes flame and heat. Frost, also called cryomancy, creates and shapes ice and cold. Aether covers everything that works on distance and boundaries: teleportation, wards and scrying.

A minor spell of any discipline costs between 5 and 15 mana. A fire bolt costs 12 mana and a frost lance costs 15 mana. Greater workings, such as summoning a storm, cost far more and are limited to Archmages.
[search_lore] passage aba95d85 (The Magic of Aethel > Mana): Mana is the energy that every spell is paid for with. A caster who cannot pay the full cost of a spell cannot cast it.

results.input: Aria's old teacher is the cruel interrogator of the Frost Wardens. Write a short, chilling monologue where he threatens a captured spy in the Ice Citadel.
results.answer:
Your lore doesn't yet name Aria's old teacher or describe Frost Warden interrogation methods. The passage says her teacher calls her the best tracker but worst at obeying orders [26e59d94]—which could give the interrogator a personal edge if he knows her. The Frost Wardens operate from the Ice Citadel [7df66575], and the Frost Binding suppresses fire magic there [275bf749], so any threat involving heat or warmth would be especially chilling in that setting.

You'll need to add details about who this teacher is and what methods he uses. What do you want to establish about him?
evidence:
[search_lore] passage 26e59d94 (Notable Characters of Aethel > Aria Voss): Aria Voss was born in a fishing village on the Northern Reach and came to the Ice Citadel at the age of twelve. She trained under the Frost Wardens and became a flint-bearer, one of the few scouts licensed to carry flint out of the Flint Vault. She is an Adept, so her mana pool holds up to 250 mana, and she can cast in both the Fire and the Frost disciplines.

Aria is patient, dry and stubborn. She keeps an oath she made as a young scout, never to leave a Warden behind in the snow. She distrusts the Ember Court and has never been to Ember Keep. Her old teacher says that she is the best tracker the Citadel has trained in thirty years, and the worst at following orders she does not agree with.
[search_lore] passage 59e8ea2e (Notable Characters of Aethel > Sera Quill): Sera Quill is an Archivist of the Glass Library and an Adept of the Aether discipline, with a pool of up to 250 mana. She came to the Library as an orphan and rose quickly through the ranks. She is curious, careful and quiet, and her work is to copy and mend the oldest texts of the Archive.

There is a rumour in the Library that Sera has read the blood-casting treatises in the Restricted Stacks. The official records say that she has never entered the Restricted Stacks, and that she holds no silver key. Sera has never confirmed or denied the rumour, and the Head Archivist has declined to comment on it.

[search_lore] passage 275bf749 (History and Factions of Aethel > The Founding of the Ice Citadel): In Year 31 the Warden-General Isolde Frane led a band of survivors north to the Northern Reach and began to build the Ice Citadel. She chose the site because the ice there was the oldest in the world and the cold slowed the wild mana that the Sundering had released. The Frost Binding, the working that smothers fire magic inside the walls, was her first great spell. She had learned it from a flint-bearer, a person who carried a flint as a token of an older craft, and she made flint the single exception to the Binding in thanks.
[search_lore] passage 7df66575 (The Ice Citadel > Overview): The Ice Citadel stands on the Northern Reach, on a spur of black rock above a frozen sea. Its walls are cut from blue glacial ice and set on foundations of dark stone. About eight hundred people live there, most of them Frost Wardens, their families and the servants who keep the Citadel running. It is the seat of the Frost Wardens and the coldest inhabited place in Aethel.

The Citadel is reached by the Gate of Frost in the western wall. The winter lasts nine months, and the Long Winter, the hardest forty days of the year, closes every road to the Citadel except the Ash Road to the south, which is usually passable.
[search_lore] passage 30ac806b (The Ice Citadel > Layout > The Flint Vault): Below the Hall of Embers is the Flint Vault, a cold cellar where the Wardens store their flint. Flint is rare in the north. The Wardens hand it out only to people they trust. A visitor can be lent a flint shard at the Gate of Frost, after signing the Ledger of Visitors, and must return the shard when leaving. Keeping a flint without permission is theft, and the punishment is a year of service in the Vault.
